summary: CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL FINDING that reframes this whole cluster: REF (Quake4Doom) is NOT a vtable-compatible adapter to the unmodified v37 SDK gamex86.dll. REF REBUILDS the game from its OWN trimmed headers (src/game/, still GAME_API_VERSION==37) and deliberately COMMENTS OUT the v37 methods it doesn't want (e.g. idCmdSystem::ArgCompletion_Models/SetupCVarsForReloadEngine/ClearCompletion, idCVarSystem::Register(idCVarHelp*)/GetHelps/the 3 memory WriteFlaggedVariables overloads, and almost the entire idSys RAVEN expansion). Because REF compiles BOTH engine and game against those trimmed headers, REF's vtables are internally consistent but do NOT match the real SDK layout. OUR project is DLL-FIRST against the UNMODIFIED v37 SDK gamex86.dll, so we CANNOT copy REF's trimmed headers for these 4 classes -- our concrete classes (idCommonLocal/idCmdSystemLocal/idCVarSystemLocal/idSysLocal) MUST present the FULL v37 SDK vtable, including every method REF stripped, or the DLL's virtual calls land on the wrong slot and crash. Use the SDK headers (c:/code/id/quake4-sdk/source/...) as the contract, REF only as a hint for WHAT a method does/whether a stub is safe. All 4 interfaces are passed by pointer in gameImport_t (sys/common/cmdSystem/cvarSystem) and are touched during GetGameAPI + game->Init(), so all are menuCritical. Good news for boot-to-menu: the game DLL calls almost none of the *new* v37 methods on the menu path -- the new slots can be pure stubs; only their PRESENCE/ORDER matters. idCVar/idCVarHelp value classes also gained data members/flags (idCVar gained SetFlag/RemoveFlag inline, non-virtual so vtable-safe; flag enum extended to BIT(24)); idCVarHelp is a brand-new value class the SDK references via idCVarSystem::Register/GetHelps.

Two interface classes analyzed: idFileSystem (framework/FileSystem.h) and idDeclManager (framework/declManager.h), plus the decl* type enum/classes they expose. Header locations: OURS = c:/code/id/DOOM-3/neo/framework/{FileSystem.h,DeclManager.h}; SDK v37 = c:/code/id/quake4-sdk/source/framework/{FileSystem.h,declManager.h}; REF = c:/code/id/_q4ref/Quake4Doom/src/framework/{FileSystem.h,declManager.h} with local impls in FileSystem.cpp / DeclManager.cpp.

KEY GROUND TRUTH (verified from SDK game.vcproj + Game_local.cpp #ifdefs): the prebuilt v37 gamex86.dll is compiled with PreprocessorDefinitions = _DEBUG/NDEBUG,_WINDOWS,GAME_DLL,Q4SDK only. RV_BINARYDECLS, RV_SINGLE_DECL_FILE, _XENON, _RV_MEM_SYS_SUPPORT are all UNDEFINED. So the canonical v37 vtables exclude every #ifdef RV_*/#if _XENON block. RegisterDeclType uses the single-allocator signature; the StartLoadingDecls/FinishLoadingDecls/LoadDeclsFromFile/WriteDeclFile/FlushDecls block is ABSENT; the trailing SetLightMaterialList/SetEntityMaterialList/PurgeType block is ABSENT. This is the exact layout to mirror.

REF is the porting template but is NOT vtable-identical to the SDK: REF builds its own DLL from its own modified declManager.h, so REF dropped SetInsideLoad/GetInsideLoad and the tools tail (GetNewName/ListDeclSummary/RemoveDeclFile/Validate/AllocateDecl) and renamed RegisterDeclFolderWrapper->RegisterDeclFolder. OUR project loads the UNMODIFIED SDK DLL, so we must match the SDK layout (which DOES include SetInsideLoad/GetInsideLoad, RegisterDeclFolderWrapper, GetNewName, AllocateDecl, etc.) — verified because the SDK game corpus calls declManager->SetInsideLoad (8x), GetInsideLoad (4x), RegisterDeclFolderWrapper (14x during Init), AllocateDecl (4x), GetNewName (2x), and fileSystem->SetIsFileLoadingAllowed (8x) and GetNewFileMemory (2x). REF's stub bodies ({return false;}/{}) still tell us WHAT a trivial stub looks like; we just need MORE slots than REF kept.

Both interfaces are heavily menuCritical: declManager->Init + RegisterDeclType/RegisterDeclFolderWrapper + SetInsideLoad run during game->Init(), and FindMaterial/FindSkin/FindSound/FindType are hit constantly during menu GUI setup; fileSystem ReadFile/ListFiles/OpenFileRead/GetNumMaps/GetMapDecl/SetIsFileLoadingAllowed run during Init and main-menu population.

New rv* types exposed only as opaque return pointers: rvDeclMatType, rvDeclLipSync, rvDeclPlayback, rvDeclEffect, rvDeclPlayerModel, rvDeclPlaybackData (REF defines all in framework/decl{MatType,LipSync,Playback}.h + DeclPlayerModel.h). Forward declarations suffice for vtable; real bodies not needed for boot-to-menu. The declType_t enum itself differs (Quake4 inserts DECL_MATERIALTYPE/LIPSYNC/PLAYBACK/EFFECT/CAMERADEF after DECL_MODELDEF and removes DECL_FX/DECL_PARTICLE) and must be ported since values cross the DLL boundary. FindDLL is byte-identical across OURS/REF (sys->DLL_GetFileName -> gamex86.dll); binary.conf is the unchanged D3 pure-mode checksum file and has NO vtable impact.

summary:
Game.h is the single most important header for the DLL-first boot. OURS is GAME_API_VERSION 8; the SDK contract is 37. Critical facts established by reading all three trees:

(1) REF's c:/code/id/_q4ref/Quake4Doom/src/game/Game.h is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the SDK's c:/code/id/quake4-sdk/source/game/Game.h. The correct port is therefore to REPLACE neo/game/Game.h's idGame/idGameEdit/gameImport_t/gameExport_t/GAME_API_VERSION with the v37 versions verbatim (modulo the build defines below).

(2) BUILD-DEFINE LANDMINE on idGame::Init (vtable slot 1, immediately after the dtor). The SDK's idlib/precompiled.h leaves _RV_MEM_SYS_SUPPORT undefined but, because ID_REDIRECT_NEWDELETE is also undefined on Windows, it DEFINES RV_UNIFIED_ALLOCATOR (precompiled.h line 70-72). Under RV_UNIFIED_ALLOCATOR the SDK's Init is `Init(void*(*allocator)(size_t), void(*deallocator)(void*), size_t(*msize)(void*))`, NOT `Init(void)`. The shipped gamex86.dll's vtable slot 1 is the 3-arg form (verified in SDK Game_local.cpp:411-414, which calls Memory::InitAllocator(allocator,deallocator,msize)). REF dodged this by COMMENTING OUT RV_UNIFIED_ALLOCATOR (REF precompiled.h:80) and recompiling both sides as Init(void) — a luxury we DON'T have since we load the prebuilt SDK DLL. Therefore OUR engine MUST define RV_UNIFIED_ALLOCATOR (or otherwise declare idGame::Init with the 3 function-pointer args) and MUST call game->Init(alloc,dealloc,msize) passing real allocator thunks (e.g. wrappers over Mem_Alloc/Mem_Free; msize via _msize). A no-arg Init() call mismatches slot 1 and crashes on the very first game call.

(3) gameImport_t grows one pointer: rvBSEManager *bse appended after collisionModelManager (since _RV_MEM_SYS_SUPPORT is OFF, the heapArena/systemHeapArray members are NOT present — import is 13 std pointers + bse). gameExport_t grows one pointer: rvGameLog *gameLog appended after gameEdit. Engine must populate gameImport.bse with a non-NULL rvBSEManager* whose vtable matches the SDK's 16-slot rvBSEManager (NOT REF's extended 20-slot one). Engine reads gameExport.game and gameExport.gameEdit and can ignore gameLog (REF's own Common.cpp ignores it; struct layout still must include the slot so the DLL's write lands correctly).

(4) idGame gained ~80 new virtuals and several signature changes interleaved THROUGHOUT the vtable (not just appended) — SetUserInfo lost canModify, added RepeaterSetUserInfo/IsClientActive early (slots ~5-6) which shift EVERYTHING after, InitFromNewMap/InitFromSaveGame dropped soundWorld, SaveGame gained saveType_t, RunFrame changed to 4 args, MenuFrame inserted, a large Repeater/* block, effects (PlayEffect/StartViewEffect), debug, ban-list, demo and loading-gui methods. Every method must be present in exact order even if stubbed.

(5) idGameEdit slot 1 (ParseSpawnArgsToRenderLight) changed return void->bool, and dozens of Raven methods (ANIM_GetAnimFromEntity, EntityGetName/ToSafeId, Script*, Thread*, mem-tracking) are inserted mid-vtable. Engine-side idGameEdit is NOT called during boot-to-menu, so a header-only layout match + trivial bodies suffice, but the LAYOUT must be exact because the same vtable is shared.

The conservative return values (Filtered=true, CanPlayRateLimited=false, ServiceEffect=true-as-expired) also keep effect-spawn paths dormant once gameplay starts, avoiding crashes from the unimplemented effect pipeline.
